what_its_for: Ofatumumab is used to treat two different conditions depending on the brand. Kesimpta is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults — this means MS that comes and goes in episodes. Arzerra is used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). This medicine works by targeting and reducing certain white blood cells called B-cells that are involved in your disease.
how_to_take: Kesimpta comes as a pre-filled autoinjector pen that you inject just under your skin (subcutaneous injection), similar to how people with diabetes inject insulin. Common injection sites are your thigh, belly (but not within 2 inches of your belly button), or outer upper arm. Rotate your injection sites each time. Arzerra is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein by a healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital setting — you cannot give this one to yourself at home. Always read the Instructions for Use that come with your medicine and ask your pharmacist or nurse to show you how to use the autoinjector if you are using Kesimpta at home.
dosing: For Kesimpta (MS): The usual starting dose is 20 mg injected under the skin once a week for the first 3 weeks (on Days 1, 7, and 14). Then, starting at Week 4 (Day 28), you switch to one injection of 20 mg once every month. Try to inject on the same day each month. For Arzerra (CLL): Dosing is determined by your doctor and given by a healthcare provider through an IV. Doses and schedules vary based on your treatment plan. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: For Kesimpta (MS): If you miss a dose during the first 3 weekly doses, contact your doctor as soon as possible for guidance. If you miss a monthly maintenance dose, inject it as soon as you remember, then continue on a new monthly schedule from that date. Do not give yourself two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For Arzerra (CLL): Your healthcare team will schedule your infusions. If you miss an appointment, call your doctor right away to reschedule.
storage: Kesimpta autoinjector pens should be stored in a refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in the original carton to protect from light. Do not freeze them — if they have been frozen, throw them away. If needed, you can keep Kesimpta at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 12 hours, but throw it away if not used within that time. Do not use if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles floating in it. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Arzerra infusion bags are prepared and stored by healthcare professionals.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive any live vaccines while taking ofatumumab and for a period after stopping — talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines. Examples of live vaccines include MMR (measles, mumps, rubella), chickenpox (varicella), and nasal flu vaccine. Avoid being around people who are sick with infections when possible, as this medicine lowers your ability to fight infections. Do not shake the Kesimpta autoinjector pen. Avoid injecting into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or scarred. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, body aches, or feeling very unwell; signs of an allergic or infusion reaction such as rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face or throat, chest tightness, or trouble breathing; unusual bruising or bleeding; sores in your mouth; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or severe stomach pain; any new or worsening neurological symptoms such as weakness, confusion, or vision changes (a rare but serious brain infection called PML can occur); or if you feel the injection site is infected (redness, warmth, swelling, or pus at the site).
when_it_works: For Kesimpta (MS): This medicine starts working to reduce B-cells in your body fairly quickly, but you may not notice changes in your MS symptoms right away. Most clinical studies showed benefits over several months of treatment. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel well, as it works to prevent future MS relapses. For Arzerra (CLL): Your cancer care team will monitor your response through blood tests and exams over weeks to months of treatment. Do not stop treatment early without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Ofatumumab may harm an unborn baby, especially if used in the second or third trimester, as it can affect the baby's immune system. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose. It is not known if ofatumumab passes into breast milk — talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Kesimpta is not currently approved for use in children. Arzerra has limited data in children. Older adults: Older patients may be at higher risk for infections — your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect how you are monitored during treatment. People with hepatitis B: Your doctor should test you for hepatitis B before starting this medicine, as it can reactivate a past hepatitis B infection, which can be serious.
